focus: Energy and commodity trade flows: what has broken in 2026 and where the barrels and cargoes went instead

routes.title: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed
routes.dateRange: Since late Feb / early Mar 2026, still live Oct 2026
routes.summary: The US–Iran war has shut most commercial traffic through Hormuz for about seven months. A June interim deal (the Islamabad MoU) briefly eased flows but did not hold. The IEA estimates oil flows through the strait averaged only 7.6 mb/d in August, 13.1 mb/d below pre-war levels, with cumulative lost exports approaching 2.8 billion barrels. More than 10 mb/d of Gulf output is shut in. Iran's new Persian Gulf Strait Authority blacklisted 45 tankers in August for breaking its transit rules (56 by early September), and US naval escorts keep part of the flow moving. Vessel transits were in single digits on several early-October days against a pre-crisis norm of ~85 a day, and tanker strikes resumed from late September. IEA members agreed a 400 million barrel emergency stock release. Brent has traded back above $100/bbl. For a trader, the questions are which barrels can still move (see the bypass pipelines entry), who replaces them (Atlantic Basin crude, Brazil, US, West Africa), and how freight and insurance reprice for the ships that do sail.
routes.source: IEA Oil Market Report, Sep 2026; CNBC 11 Sep 2026; IMF PortWatch via straits.live, Oct 2026; marinelink.com; bairdmaritime.com (2026)

routes.title: Hormuz bypass pipelines: Yanbu and Fujairah
routes.dateRange: Mar–Oct 2026; East-West line hit in early Sep
routes.summary: Only two pipelines get Gulf crude out without passing Hormuz. Saudi Arabia's East-West line to Yanbu on the Red Sea ramped up to about 5 mb/d (versus ~0.8 mb/d before the crisis), and the UAE's Habshan–Fujairah line exits below the strait. Analysts point to port loading capacity, not pipe capacity, as the binding limit. Then attacks shut the East-West pipeline in early September, cutting the main bypass. Barrels that do reach Yanbu must still pass a Red Sea where the Houthis are blockading Saudi-linked shipping (next entry), so the bypass is only as good as the next chokepoint.
routes.source: IEA Oil Market Report, Sep 2026; IEA Strait of Hormuz factsheet, Feb 2026; trade press, Oct 2026

routes.title: Qatar LNG force majeure: a global gas shock
routes.summary: About 93% of Qatar's and 96% of the UAE's LNG exports pass through Hormuz, roughly 19% of global LNG trade, and none of it has a pipeline bypass. Qatar declared force majeure in March, and its exports were down ~96% year on year by August. European gas (TTF) more than doubled to roughly €70–77/MWh in late August–early September, a three-year high. Asian buyers lost their largest long-term supplier and bid against Europe for spot cargoes. US Gulf Coast LNG (a record 109 Mt in 2025) became the marginal supplier to both, which is why Panama Canal slots and Atlantic freight suddenly matter so much.
routes.source: EIA Today in Energy (2026); IEA Strait of Hormuz factsheet; GIIGNL Annual Report 2026; trade press Sep 2026

routes.title: Red Sea: Houthi attacks resumed, Cape detour continues
routes.dateRange: Since 2024; attacks resumed Feb 2026; Saudi blockade since Jul 2026
routes.summary: The Houthis' 2025 pause ended at the end of February 2026, when they announced renewed attacks on Red Sea shipping, linked to the strikes on Iran. In July they declared a complete naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, aimed squarely at the oil Saudi Arabia was rerouting to Yanbu to avoid Hormuz. In September they seized the port of Mokha, Perim island inside the Bab-el-Mandeb strait and the Hanish islands. On 4 October Saudi-backed Yemeni forces launched a counter-offensive and claimed control of the strait, so the situation is fluid. Around 30 tankers near Yanbu sit within Houthi strike range. Most Asia–Europe tankers and container ships still go round the Cape, adding about 10–14 days. That ties up ships and lifts freight rates on every route, not just this one.
routes.source: CNN (4 Oct 2026); Euronews (14 Sep 2026); CNBC (22 Jul 2026); CFR; Lloyd's List Intelligence Red Sea brief (Aug 2026)

routes.title: Panama Canal: El Niño drought caps transits
routes.dateRange: Restrictions Aug–Oct 2026; partial easing from 15 Oct
routes.summary: A severe El Niño cut rainfall in the canal watershed roughly 34% below average from May to August. The canal authority imposed its first daily transit cap since the 2023–24 crisis: 34 ships a day from 3 September, then 32 from 15 September (versus a normal ~36), together with draught cuts. From 15 October the Neopanamax locks go from 9 to 10 daily transits (33 a day in total), but capacity stays below normal. Demand is unusually high: laden LNG transits hit a two-year high in June as US cargoes chased Asian prices after the loss of Qatari supply, and an LPG carrier slot sold at auction for a record $5.3 million on 1 September. VLGC (LPG) freight rates hit record highs.
routes.source: S&P Global Commodity Insights (Jul 2026); FreightWaves; Marine Insight; Maritime Executive; Hellenic Shipping News (Sep 2026)

routes.title: Russian crude: shadow fleet to India and China
routes.summary: Russia ships roughly 3.8–4.1 mb/d of crude by sea; China takes ~51% and India ~38%. In March 2026 almost half of Russia's seaborne oil moved on sanctioned 'shadow' tankers, 92% of them over 15 years old, and Western governments have now sanctioned 651 tankers. The share exported by US-designated producers (Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazpromneft, Surgutneftegaz) fell to 4–8% in Q1 2026, then recovered to 57% by mid-May. India's imports of Russian crude doubled month on month in March, as Gulf supply was shut in. With the Red Sea unsafe, Baltic cargoes to India increasingly go round Africa.
routes.source: KSE Institute Russian Oil Tracker (May 2026); CREA monthly analysis (Mar 2026)

routes.title: Petrochemicals: China flips from PE/PP importer to exporter
routes.summary: From the original Tricon-prep version of this map, kept because it is a demand-side story, not a transport one. China's PE/PP imports hit record lows in April 2026 while its PE exports hit record highs (+122% YoY), squeezing the export markets that ~3.3 Mt/yr of new US Gulf Coast PE capacity (Shell, Baystar, Nova, Dow) built since 2023 was counting on.
